title: A Software Caching Runtime for Embedded NVRAM Systems
problem: Resource-constrained microcontrollers struggle to efficiently support advanced workloads for IoT and edge computing due to memory limitations. Emerging NVRAM technologies require software abstractions to effectively manage memory hierarchies and enable high-performance data processing on low-power devices.
motivation: IoT and edge devices increasingly demand sophisticated data collection, processing, and inference capabilities within strict power and memory constraints.
method: The paper presents a software caching layer for microcontrollers equipped with NVRAM (non-volatile RAM—memory that keeps data even when powered off). The runtime works like a smart traffic controller, automatically moving data between the microcontroller's limited fast memory and the larger NVRAM storage based on what the program needs. By taking advantage of NVRAM's ability to save program state without draining power, the system enables memory-limited devices to handle large-scale data storage and processing while maintaining ultra-low-power operation.
key_novelty: This paper introduces a software caching system designed for microcontrollers with NVRAM, using the memory's non-volatility (ability to keep data when powered off) to enable large-scale storage and processing on memory-limited devices.
contributions: Software caching runtime optimized for embedded NVRAM systems
Program state non-volatility mechanisms for ultra-low-power microcontrollers
Support for large-scale data processing and inference on resource-constrained edge nodes
primary_theme: Software caching runtime for NVRAM embedded systems
